text: {"skills":[{"skill_id":"ionicity_ladder_wide_gap_chemistry_v2","rules":[{"rule_id":"closed_shell_ionic_halide","conditions":{"anion_family":"halide","transition_metal_flag":"no_transition_metal"},"weight":0.7,"rationale":"Main-group halides are maximally ionic with closed-shell cations; no d-states in gap, giving the widest experimental gaps."},{"rule_id":"oxide_deep_o2p_valence_band","conditions":{"anion_family":"oxide"},"weight":0.4,"rationale":"Strong ionicity and deep O 2p valence band place oxides high on the electronegativity-difference gap ladder."},{"rule_id":"partially_filled_d_band_narrowing","conditions":{"transition_metal_flag":"has_transition_metal"},"weight":-0.3,"rationale":"Partially filled d bands introduce states near the Fermi level, narrowing or closing gaps; source evidence here was near-zero confidence."},{"rule_id":"pnictide_covalent_narrow_gap","conditions":{"anion_family":"pnictide"},"weight":-0.3,"rationale":"Pnictides are weakly ionic covalent semiconductors; small electronegativity difference yields small experimental gaps."}],"ridge":0.8,"prior_scale":0.6,"semantic_mass_start":0.55,"semantic_mass_end":0.2,"ucb_weight":0.55,"gp_beta_start":2.0,"gp_beta_end":0.9,"gp_xi":0.03,"confidence":0.65,"hypothesis":"Ranks anion chemistry by cation-anion electronegativity difference and downweights the near-zero-confidence transition-metal source relation. Fails for d0 transition-metal oxides and heavily distorted or defect-dominated experimental structures where measured gaps deviate from ionicity ordering."},{"skill_id":"chalcogenide_polarizability_narrow_gap_counter_hypothesis","rules":[{"rule_id":"chalcogenide_polarizable_valence_band","conditions":{"anion_family":"chalcogenide"},"weight":-0.5,"rationale":"S/Se/Te p-states raise the valence band, shrinking the gap; source chalcogenide effect was positive on refractive index."},{"rule_id":"metalloid_covalent_semiconductor_penalty","conditions":{"dominant_family":"metalloid"},"weight":-0.45,"rationale":"Covalent metalloid networks are classic narrow-gap semiconductors; largest source effect on refractive index."},{"rule_id":"heavy_mean_z_diffuse_orbital_penalty","conditions":{"mean_atomic_number_bin":"mean_z_high"},"weight":-0.4,"rationale":"Heavy-atom diffuse orbitals broaden the conduction band, reducing the measured gap."},{"rule_id":"halide_closed_shell_wide_gap","conditions":{"anion_family":"halide"},"weight":0.55,"rationale":"Closed-shell halides lack d-states in the gap, giving wider experimental gaps than polarizable chalcogenides."}],"ridge":1.0,"prior_scale":0.4,"semantic_mass_start":0.4,"semantic_mass_end":0.15,"ucb_weight":0.6,"gp_beta_start":2.2,"gp_beta_end":1.0,"gp_xi":0.02,"confidence":0.5,"hypothesis":"Keeps the chalcogenide and metalloid penalties but drops the Moss inversion and the low-confidence heavy-Z penalty. Fails if the target pool contains few chalcogenides or metalloids, or if halide candidates are rare or defective."}],"selected_skill_id":"ionicity_ladder_wide_gap_chemistry_v2","lesson":"Across eight development seeds the two skills had similar mean AUCs (65.3 vs 72.7) and final best scores (84.4 vs 84.6), so neither is clearly superior. The ionicity-ladder skill reached 100% on five seeds while the inverted-transfer skill peaked at 100% on four, suggesting both are useful diagnostics but the ionicity ordering is the safer frozen deployment.","revision_summary":"Retained the ionicity-ladder skill with the same rules, parameters, and hypothesis, only changing the version number to v2. Replaced the inverted-transfer skill with a counter-hypothesis that keeps the chalcogenide and metalloid penalties but drops the Moss inversion and the low-confidence heavy-Z penalty, and lowered its semantic mass to 0.4 start/0.15 end. Selected the ionicity-ladder skill for deployment. Used only exact catalog field-value pairs, kept rationales under 25 words and hypotheses under 45 words, and kept all parameters within allowed ranges."}

{"skills":[{"skill_id":"ionicity_ladder_wide_gap_chemistry_v3","rules":[{"rule_id":"closed_shell_ionic_halide","conditions":{"anion_family":"halide","transition_metal_flag":"no_transition_metal"},"weight":0.7,"rationale":"Main-group halides are maximally ionic with closed-shell cations; no d-states in gap, giving the widest experimental gaps."},{"rule_id":"oxide_deep_o2p_valence_band","conditions":{"anion_family":"oxide"},"weight":0.45,"rationale":"Strong ionicity and deep O 2p valence band place oxides high on the electronegativity-difference gap ladder."},{"rule_id":"chalcogenide_polarizable_narrow_gap","conditions":{"anion_family":"chalcogenide"},"weight":-0.4,"rationale":"Polarizable S/Se/Te p-states raise the valence band and shrink gaps; the largest anion population needs an explicit penalty."},{"rule_id":"lanthanide_fully_filled_4f_wide_gap","conditions":{"lanthanide_flag":"has_lanthanide"},"weight":0.3,"rationale":"Fully filled 4f orbitals add no gap-narrowing states; lanthanide ionicity raises measured gaps."}],"ridge":0.9,"prior_scale":0.55,"semantic_mass_start":0.5,"semantic_mass_end":0.2,"ucb_weight":0.55,"gp_beta_start":2.0,"gp_beta_end":0.9,"gp_xi":0.03,"confidence":0.65,"hypothesis":"Ranks anion chemistry by cation-anion electronegativity difference, rewarding ionic halides and oxides while penalizing polarizable chalcogenides, and adds lanthanide ionicity support. Fails for d0 transition-metal oxides and defect-dominated experimental structures deviating from ionicity ordering."},{"skill_id":"moss_inverted_transfer_with_chalcogenide_downweight","rules":[{"rule_id":"halide_low_polarizability_wide_gap","conditions":{"anion_family":"halide"},"weight":0.6,"rationale":"Halides had the most negative source refractive-index effect; low polarizability inverts to wide experimental band gaps via Moss."},{"rule_id":"metalloid_covalent_semiconductor_penalty","conditions":{"dominant_family":"metalloid"},"weight":-0.5,"rationale":"Largest source refractive-index effect; covalent metalloid networks are classic narrow-gap semiconductors under Moss inversion."},{"rule_id":"heavy_mean_z_diffuse_orbital_penalty","conditions":{"mean_atomic_number_bin":"mean_z_high"},"weight":-0.35,"rationale":"High mean-Z boosted source refractive index; diffuse heavy-atom orbitals increase bandwidth and reduce band gap."},{"rule_id":"chalcogenide_source_confidence_downweight","conditions":{"anion_family":"chalcogenide"},"weight":0.1,"rationale":"Source chalcogenide effect was near zero; low confidence justifies a near-neutral rather than a negative weight."}],"ridge":1.1,"prior_scale":0.45,"semantic_mass_start":0.4,"semantic_mass_end":0.15,"ucb_weight":0.6,"gp_beta_start":2.1,"gp_beta_end":1.0,"gp_xi":0.02,"confidence":0.5,"hypothesis":"Counter-hypothesis blending Moss-inverted source penalties on metalloids and heavy-Z with a near-neutral chalcogenide term and halide reward. Fails where high index and wide gap coexist in ionic heavy oxides, or low source confidence misleads inversion."}],"selected_skill_id":"ionicity_ladder_wide_gap_chemistry_v3","lesson":"Across two generations of development seeds, the ionicity ladder skill maintained a higher mean AUC (72.7 then 81.3) than the Moss-inverted transfer (65.3 then 73.5), and both shared hard seeds (229102/229104 and 229109/229110), so task variance rather than skill flaws explains the spread. I keep the domain-grounded ionicity ladder for deployment, add lanthanide ionicity support, and drop the low-confidence d-band rule. The second skill is a Moss-inverted counter-hypothesis with the near-zero-confidence chalcogenide relation downweighted to near neutral rather than negative.","revision_summary":"Kept exactly two skills with four rules each, converted conditions to catalog-field-to-value maps, and preserved the ionicity ladder as deployment with added lanthanide support and dropped d-band rule. The second skill is a Moss-inverted counter-hypothesis with the near-zero-confidence chalcogenide relation downweighted to near neutral rather than negative. All parameters stay within allowed ranges; no target outcomes or candidate identifiers are referenced, and feedback was used only for relative ranking, not causal mechanism claims from eight seeds per generation."}

{"skills":[{"skill_id":"polar_hbond_hydration_core","rules":[{"rule_id":"heteroatom_rich_polarity","conditions":{"hetero_atom_bin":"hetero_high"},"weight":0.7,"rationale":"Hydration free energy is driven by N/O hydrogen bonding with water; fails if polarity terms carry the signal or if the small hetero_high bin is informative."}],"selected_skill_id":"polar_hbond_hydration_core","lesson":"Across eight development seeds the polarity skill led the size-transfer skill by 20.6 AUC points (74.5 vs 53.9), so polarity is the safer prior even though both skills decay semantic mass toward the target-only anchor.","revision_summary":"Kept the deployed polarity skill intact and replaced the downweighted short-length rule with an acyclic bonus, then added a counter-hypothesis that keeps the low-confidence ESOL length priors and downweights hetero_high polarity. The polarity skill remains frozen for deployment."}
